content: Nucleolar protein with MIF4G domain 1 (NOM1) is a protein encoded by the NOM1 gene in humans. Proteins that contain MIF4G (middle of eIF4G) and/or MA3 domains, such as NOM1, play a role in the process of protein translation. These domains serve as binding sites for members of the EIF4A family, which are ATP-dependent DEAD box RNA helicases. To study the function of NOM1, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, designated as Nom1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases for research purposes. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of NOM1 gene deletion. A total of 25 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and three significant abnormalities were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, indicating that they did not survive to the weaning stage. The remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice. Among these, female mice exhibited an abnormal hair cycle.
